content: Estrogens, when used alone or in combination with another hormone like progestin, can sometimes lead to serious side effects. It is important to discuss the risks and benefits of hormone therapy with your doctor. Estrogens may increase the risk of uterine cancer (endometrial cancer). Taking a progestin as directed by your doctor can help reduce this risk. In postmenopausal women, estrogens, whether taken with or without progestin, can increase the risk of breast or ovarian cancer, stroke, dementia, and serious blood clots. The likelihood of these serious side effects depends on the dose of estrogen and the duration of its use. This medication should be used at the lowest effective dose and for the shortest possible time. Regular check-ins with your doctor (e.g., every 3 to 6 months) are recommended to assess whether continued use is necessary. If long-term use is required, annual physical exams, including breast exams, mammograms, pelvic exams, and Pap smears, should be conducted as directed by your doctor. This medication is a hormone (estrogen) used by women to alleviate menopause symptoms such as hot flashes and vaginal dryness, which occur due to reduced estrogen production in the body. Certain estrogen products may also be used postmenopause to prevent bone loss (osteoporosis). However, other medications like raloxifene or bisphosphonates (e.g., alendronate) may be safer and equally effective for preventing bone loss. Before starting this medication, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Take the medication orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor. If you are prescribed extended-release tablets, do not crush, chew, or dissolve them, as this can release the drug all at once, increasing the risk of side effects. Take the medication regularly to maximize its benefits, and try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Follow your dosing schedule carefully. Common side effects may include stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, bloating, breast tenderness, headache, or weight changes. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor believes the benefits outweigh the risks. Rarely, this medication may cause serious, sometimes fatal, blood clot-related problems such as heart attack, stroke, or clots in the lungs or legs. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Before taking this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Avoid smoking or using tobacco while on this medication, as it increases the risk of blood clots. Inform your doctor if you have recently had or will be undergoing surgery, or if you will be confined to a chair or bed for an extended period (e.g., during a long flight), as these conditions increase the risk of blood clots, especially when taking estrogen products. This medication may cause blotchy, dark areas on the skin (melasma). Sunlight can worsen this effect, so limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen. If you are nearsighted or wear contact lenses, you may experience vision problems or difficulty wearing your lenses. Children may be more sensitive to the side effects of this drug, which could affect their growth and development. This medication should not be used during pregnancy. It passes into breast milk and may reduce the quality and quantity of milk produced. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, nonprescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests (e.g., metyrapone test), potentially causing false results. If someone overdoses and has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Engaging in mental exercises (e.g., reading, solving puzzles) can help prevent dementia. To promote healthy bones, increase weight-bearing exercise, quit smoking, limit alcohol intake, and consume a well-balanced diet with adequate calcium and vitamin D. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Properly discard expired or unused medication. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. For disposal instructions, consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
